section.title: Introduction
section.p: The Window Manager has been updated to provide notifications of the pointer entering and leaving icons. These transition messages are similar to those provided by the 'pointer entering/leaving window' messages. Most clients will not need to receive such notifications.

subsection.title: Wimp_Poll reason codes and masks
subsection.p: The new reasons codes have been allocated as event codes 14 (pointer leaving icon) and 15 (pointer entering icon). Because most applications will not have these bits masked in their Wimp_Poll mask it is necessary to set bit 25 in the mask to indicate that the events are required. Thus, the mask definition has been updated to add the following bits :

bitfield-table.bit: If set, ignore 'pointer leaving icon' events
If set, ignore 'pointer entering icon' events
If clear, ignore all 'pointer entering/leaving icon' events; if set, obey bits 14 and 15

subsection.p: Wimp_Poll event codes 14 and 15 are returned whenever the above conditions have been met, and the mouse has moved in or out of an icon's bounding box.
Event codes 14 and 15 return the same structure in the user's event block :

Icon transition events will never be returned for the logical window background, which is usually indicated by icon handle -1. When windows are closed beneath the pointer the events will be delivered in the logical manner as if the pointer had left the window naturally. Thus, the usual sequence of events for a pointer moving into a window, to a 'Close' button, and clicking it would be :

item.p: Pointer entering close icon [mouse clicked, window closed]
